def: The Jenkins server that holds the jobs, settings, credentials and history, and hands builds to agents. It shouldn't run builds itself.
A machine that runs builds for the controller. Agents can be added, replaced or thrown away.
The folder where Jenkins keeps everything: jobs, build history, plugins and credentials. Back it up.
Where Jenkins keeps secrets such as tokens, encrypted, so pipelines can use them without the values appearing in code or logs.
A file in the repository that describes a pipeline as code, so it's reviewed and versioned like everything else.
The structured Jenkinsfile style that starts with pipeline { and uses fixed sections: agent, stages, steps, environment, when and post.
A Jenkins job that finds every branch and pull request in a repository and runs its Jenkinsfile for each one.
A message a service like GitHub sends to another system when something happens, such as a push, so builds start at once.
Jenkins pipeline code kept in its own repository and reused by many Jenkinsfiles, so common steps are written once.
Merging small changes often, with every change built and tested automatically before it can join the main branch.
Keeping every change that passes the pipeline ready for production, so releasing is a routine, repeatable step.
The sha256 fingerprint of an image's contents. Unlike a tag, it always means exactly one image.
Moving the same, already-tested artifact to the next environment, instead of building it again.
A few quick checks right after a deploy that the release really runs in that environment.
A pause in a pipeline where a person must agree before it continues, usually before production, with a time limit.
Safe to run more than once: running it twice gives the same result as running it once.
The numbers, agreed before a release, that make a canary stop and roll back: error rate, latency, minimum sample and bake time.
How long each canary step runs before it's judged, so slow-appearing problems have time to show.
